title: Nanosensors to Detect Protease Activity In Vivo for Noninvasive Diagnostics
protocol: Chill 1 mL of 30% ammonium hydroxide in an ice bucket for 30 minutes.
Wash a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask with deionized water and add 10 mL double distilled water (ddH2O).
Submerge the outside of the flask in an ice bath resting on a stir/heat plate.
Use a plastic pipette to flow N2 gas into the ddH2O in the flask.
Bubble for 15 minutes with N2 to deoxygenate.
Weigh 224 μmol (4.5 grams) of dextran (Molecular Weight (MW) = 20 kDa) into a 50 mL conical tube.
Add H2O such that the final volume of the mixture, including the dextran, is 20 mL.
Vortex vigorously to dissolve the dextran.
Weigh 290 µmol of iron(III) chloride hexahydrate and add to dextran solution.
Vortex to dissolve iron(III) chloride in dextran solution.
Filter the resulting solution through a 0.2 µm filter.
Transfer 1 mL chilled ammonium hydroxide into 9 mL deoxygenated water.
Weigh 367 µmol of iron(II) chloride tetrahydrate and dissolve in 1 mL oxygen-free ddH2O.
Filter the iron(II) solution through a 0.2 µm filter.
Transfer dextran-iron(III) solution into a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Deoxygenate the flask with N2 for 15 minutes on ice.
Cap the flask with a rubber septum and puncture it with an 18 gauge needle to flow N2.
Insert another 18 gauge needle as a flow outlet for gas.
Add 467 µL of iron(II) solution to dextran-iron(III) solution with a syringe, stirring at 1600 rpm.
Initiate the nucleation process by adding chilled dilute ammonium hydroxide dropwise into Iron(II)-Iron(III)-dextran solution.
Ensure each droplet mixes well before dropping in another until 1-2 mL of ammonium hydroxide is added.
Stop the flow of N2 and remove the rubber septum.
Remove the ice bath and replace with a warm water bath, continuing to stir the solution.
Ensure that the temperature of the solution reaches 75°C and incubate for 75 minutes.
Remove the flask from the stir/hot plate and filter the solution through a 0.2 µm filter followed by a 0.1 µm filter to remove coarse particles.
Buffer exchange the filtered particles into ddH2O using 100 kDa molecular weight cut-off concentrators to remove excess dextran.
Centrifuge at 4°C at 4800 X g for 15 minutes, discard the flow-through, and add new buffer to the IONP solution. Repeat 3-5 times if necessary.
Determine the concentration of the nanoparticles using a spectrophotometer/plate reader by taking absorbance measurements at 400 nm with ε = 2.07 x 106 cm-1 M-1.
Resuspend the IONPs to 10 mg/mL in ddH2O, ensuring the total volume is ~3 mL and using polypropylene tubes for chemical compatibility.
Add 1.6 volumes of 5 M NaOH to the resuspended IONPs.
Add 0.65 volumes of epichlorohydrin to the solution containing NaOH.
Mix rigorously on a plate shaker at room temperature for 12 hours to crosslink dextran.
Use a 20 mL syringe with an 18-gauge needle to transfer the IONP solution into the 50 kDa m.w.c.o. dialysis membrane.
Place the dialysis membrane into 4 L ddH2O and replace H2O every 2-3 hours for overnight incubation.
Measure the concentration of IONPs and adjust to 5 mg/mL.
Add ammonium hydroxide to reach 20% (v/v).
Shake at room temperature for more than 12 hours.
Buffer exchange using 30 kDa m.w.c.o. filters.
Adjust the volume down to 2.5 - 3.5 mL before purification by Fast Protein Liquid Chromatography (FPLC).
Use dynamic light scattering (DLS) to determine the hydrodynamic radius of IONPs, with an expected range of 10-100 nm and average size of 40-50 nm.
Store IONPs at 4°C.
Synthesize a peptide substrate for the target protease with an N-terminal fluorescent reporter such as Fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) and a C-terminal cysteine residue.
Aliquot 0.5 mg of IONP at 1 mg/mL into coupling buffer using a spin filter.
Dissolve Succinimidyl iodoacetate (SIA) in dimethylformamide (DMF) to reach a concentration of ~30 mg/mL.
Add SIA to IONP at a mole ratio of 500 SIA:IONP.
Incubate the mixture for 1 - 2 hours at room temperature in the dark.
Buffer exchange using a spin filter into coupling buffer to remove unreacted SIA.
Mix the peptide of interest at a molar ratio of 90:1 (peptide:IONP) with thiol-terminated polyethylene glycol (PEG) at a molar ratio of 20:1 (PEG:IONP).
Combine this peptide-PEG solution with IONP.
Incubate overnight at room temperature on a plate shaker, covering tubes in foil to prevent photobleaching.
Add L-cysteine at a molar ratio of 500:1 (C:IONP) to neutralize any unreacted SIA molecules.
Incubate for 1 hour at 25°C on a shaker at highest speed at room temperature.
Purify via FPLC.
Use a spectrophotometer to measure the absorbance of the sample solution at 400 nm (Asample,400).
Measure the absorbance of the sample solution at the wavelength of maximum absorbance for the fluorophore used, which is 488 nm for FITC (Asample,488).
Measure the absorbance of a stock amine IONP solution at 400 nm and 488 nm.
Calculate the normalized A400 value using Equation 1.
Calculate the normalized A488 value using Equation 2.
Use the values from Equations 1 and 2 to calculate the Peptide:IONP ratio with Equation 3.
Store product at 1 mg/mL at 4°C in PBS after purification.
Make an 18 µL nanoparticle solution with a 200 nM concentration of peptide in PBS (1% BSA).
Mix the nanoparticle solution with 2 µL of protease of interest (MMP9; 0.1 - 1 mg/mL).
Incubate the mixture in a plate reader at 37 °C for 1 hour.
Take fluorescence measurements every 1 to 2 minutes using an excitation wavelength of 485 nm and emission wavelength of 528 nm.
Create a metabolic cage for urine collection by securing a cylindrical sleeve to the top of a 96 well plate.
Place a mouse inside the sleeve during urine collection.
Cover the mouse with a Petri dish cover to prevent escape.
Prepare an injection solution containing nanosensors in sterile saline.
Administer the nanosensor solution via tail vein injection into female, 8-week old, nude mice bearing xenograft LS174T colorectal tumors.
Place mice into metabolic cages immediately after injection and note the time of injection for each mouse.
Remove cylindrical sleeve from 96-well plate at 60 - 90 minutes post-injection.
Restrain mouse and apply slight pressure on the bladder to induce urination onto the plate.
Collect urine samples (200 - 500 µL) for analysis by immunoprecipitation.
Wash magnetic beads 3 times with coating buffer, bringing final volume to 225 µL.
Prepare fresh coating buffer (0.1 M sodium borate, pH 9.5), blocking buffer (PBS, 0.5% BSA, 0.05% Tween-20, pH 7.4), and washing buffer (PBS, 0.1% BSA, 0.05% Tween-20, pH 7.4).
Add 200 µL of anti-FITC (5 mg/mL) to the magnetic beads.
Incubate with ammonium sulfate (3 M) for 16-24 hours at 37°C on a rotator.
Add the solution to a magnetic separator.
Remove the supernatant.
Replace with 625 µL blocking buffer.
Incubate at 37°C overnight.
Wash three times with wash buffer.
Store in 1.25 mL wash buffer.
Incubate 2 µL of urine with 5 µL of magnetic beads (20 mg/mL).
Bring the total volume to 50 µL with PBS (0.01% Tween 20).
Incubate for 60 min.
Wash twice with 50 µL PBS (0.01% Tween 20) using a magnetic separator after each wash.
Elute twice with 32.5 µL of 5% glacial Acetic Acid.
Neutralize pooled elution (70 µL) with 35 µL of 2 M Tris to achieve a final pH of ~7.
Read on a plate reader at appropriate excitation and emission wavelengths to quantify urine fluorescence.
Calculate the concentration of fluorescent reporter against a ladder of known concentrations of free fluorophore.
